lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Reteach and varied practice: reading and writing numerical expressions

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: These two examples show the same idea in two different formats.

items.prompt: Describe 5 × (12 + 3) in words without evaluating it.

steps: The parentheses show that 12 and 3 are added first.
workedSolution.answer: Add 12 and 3, then multiply the sum by 5.

items.prompt: Let E represent 18 + 7. Without evaluating, compare 4 × (18 + 7) with E.

steps: The parentheses contain the same expression represented by E.
The factor 4 multiplies that entire expression, so the new expression is 4 times E.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A supply cart has 9 boxes with 6 markers in each box and 3 loose markers. Which expression represents the total number of markers?
A garden has 5 trays with 11 seedlings in each tray and 9 extra seedlings. How many seedlings are there in all?
In 188111, how does the value of the 8 in the ten-thousands place compare with the value of the 8 in the thousands place?
Round each number to the nearest hundred to estimate 5049 + 7367.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Round 23 to the nearest ten and 49 to the nearest ten, then multiply to estimate the product.
A student says 4693 - 1449 = 3344. Round each number to the nearest hundred. Which choice correctly checks the claim?
choices: The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 3300.
The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 3400.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 3244 and the rounded estimate is 3300.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 3244 and the rounded estimate is 3400.

items.prompt: A student evaluates [56 + 11] × 7 - 7: “They multiply 11 by 7 first, then finish the calculation, so the value is 126.” Which statement best identifies the error?
choices: The work is correct; 126 is the value.
The student multiplied before evaluating [56 + 11]; the grouped sum is 67, giving 462.
The grouping symbols do not affect the order; 126 is the value.
The student used the right first step but made an arithmetic slip; the value should be 464.

items.prompt: A student says, “In 3341972, the value of the 3 in the hundred-thousands place is the same value as the value of the 3 in the millions place.” Which statement best analyzes the error?
choices: The values are 300000 and 3000000; 300000 is the same value as 3000000, so the student's comparison is correct.
Both digits have value 3; repeated digits always have the same value.
The values are 300000 and 3000000; 300000 is 1/10 as much as 3000000, so the student's comparison is incorrect.
The values are 300000 and 3000000; 300000 is 10 times as much as 3000000.
